Full text: OPERATOR: Good evening, ladies and gentlemen. I am Pratibha, the moderator for this conference. Welcome to the TCS conference call. [OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS] I would now like to hand over to the TCS management. Thank you and over to TCS. DAVID NELSON, HEAD OF GLOBAL INVESTOR RELATIONS, TATA CONSULTANCY SERVICES: Thank you. Good evening and good morning. Welcome, everyone. And thank you for joining us on the TCS earnings call for quarter four and for the fiscal year 2007. I am David Nelson, Head of Global Investor Relations. Please note that this call is being webcast through our website, which is www.tcs.com. And an archive, including transcript, will be available on the site for the duration of the quarter. The financial statements, results presentation, and press release are also available on our website. Our leadership team is present on this call to discuss our results. We have with us Mr. Ramadorai, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director. SUBRAMANIAN RAMADORAI, CEO AND MANAGING DIRECTOR, TATA CONSULTANCY SERVICES: Good evening, everyone. DAVID NELSON: Mr. Mahalingam, Chief Financial Officer. SETURAMAN MAHALINGAM, CFO, TATA CONSULTANCY SERVICES: Good evening. DAVID NELSON: We also have our three Executive Vice Presidents, Mr. Chandrasekaran, Head of Global Sales and Operations. N. CHANDRASEKARAN, HEAD OF GLOBAL SALES AND OPERATIONS, TATA CONSULTANCY SERVICES: Good evening, and good morning. DAVID NELSON: Mr. Padmanabhan, Head of Global Human Resources. SHAMALA PADMANABHAN, HEAD OF GLOBAL HUMAN RESOURCES, TATA CONSULTANCY SERVICES: Hello, everyone. DAVID NELSON: And Mr. Phiroz Vandrevala, Head of Global Corporate Affairs. PHIROZ VANDREVALA, HEAD OF GLOBAL CORPORATE AFFAIRS, TATA CONSULTANCY SERVICES: Hi, everyone. DAVID NELSON: Mr. Ramadorai and Mr. Mahalingam will begin with a brief overview of the company's performance, followed by the Q&A session. As you are aware, TCS does not provide specific revenue and earnings guidance. Furthermore, anything said on this call, which reflects our outlook for the future, which can be construed as a forward-looking statement, must be viewed in conjunction with the risks that the company faces. These risks are outlined

on the second slide of our results presentation. With that, I would like to turn the call over to Mr. Ramadorai. SUBRAMANIAN RAMADORAI: Thank you, David. And let me a few moments to describe the overall performance of the company for the year 2006-2007, as well as for the quarter. This has been a standout year for TCS. We have very clearly demonstrated industry leadership and excellence in execution. Where we need to provide it, we have provided our customers with certainty in running and transforming their business. The full year revenues, we clocked around $4.3 billion and an operating income of $1.1 billion, and essentially a 41% year-on-year growth which is very important. TCS North America and TCS Europe have crossed the US$2 billion and $1 billion in terms of revenues, Europe being $1 billion and North American being $2 billion. In terms of our quarter four revenues, that is the January through March '07, there were revenues of $1.2 billion, driven by a quarter-on-quarter growth rate of 8% in dollar terms, is extremely heartening. We are seeing for the 2007-2008 a good ramp up on our existing deals which we have won, and a good demand environment across the geographies. More importantly, demand for our technology-led solutions from our global customers. I think the strength of our business models in terms of an integrated, full-services player and a global network delivery model, enables us to address very complex engagements, win large complex global engagements which we can deliver out of our global network delivery centers. Last year, namely the 06/07, the strength of this model helped us to close 12 $50-million plus deals across all the major markets. And we have managed our operations very well with regard to a strong financial management. And despite the constant gyration of the Indian currency, we have done very well. We added 32,000 professionals at a gross level. And our retention has been the highest in the industry. And we will answer any questions. Overall, the attrition on a global basis was 11.3%. With regard to the branding campaign, which we

started this year, that's what we want our customers to know us about, and what we stand for in terms of our customers' experience in certainty and in information technology. We are building the TCS brand globally and better communicate our commitment to the customers and prospects. Just four years ago, in 2003, we were the first Indian IT company to cross the $1-billion revenue mark. We doubled our revenues in 2005. And once again, we have replicated that in 2007 by crossing US$4 billion in terms of revenue. Our business model, to sum up, is primed for profitable growth. And there's no dearth of opportunities out there. I'll hand over to Mr. Mahalingam, our Chief Financial Officer. SETURAMAN MAHALINGAM: Thank you, Ram. At the close of the 2007 financial year, we have, as you have heard from Ram, and I'm sure you've accessed our website, we have delivered again very strong financial results. We are now the first head for India, headquartered IT services company to exceed $4 billion in revenue, after-tax profits of nearly $1 billion. This continued strong growth reflects the strength of customer demand for our services. Ram has already indicated that we have witnessed an increasing acceptance of our strategy to provide our clients with comprehensive and integrated portfolio of services delivered over a global delivery network. For the full year, as you I'm sure have seen, our revenue has reached $4.3 billion, a 41% increase over FY 2006. For the quarter, revenue has grown sequentially 8% in U.S. dollar terms and 6% in rupee terms. Since I know that I'll get a lot of questions on the details of the revenue, let me provide the following breakdown. Our revenue went up by 5.88% over Q3. And this has come about as a result of volume growth of 6.42%, pricing growth of 89 basis points, improvement in mix and productivity of 44 basis points, and of course the exchange difference has had a negative effect of 1.87% which has resulted into a 5.88% growth. As we've always repeated, our goal is not just to grow

but also growth in sustainable profitability. Despite the challenging environment, the significant cost pressure that we have seen on volatile currency market, our results have demonstrated this capability. Let me walk you through the details of the items that have affected Q4 margins, because there's been largely one. As you know, we exited Q3 with an operating margin of 26.07%. And there has been a negative foreign exchange impact of [57] basis points in our margin. But in spite of that, we have improved the [inaudible] in a marginal manner which has resulted in the Q4 operating margin of 25.59%. On a year-to-year basis, we have run several successive programs that control cost and expense. Non-employee SG&A has shown an improvement of 102 basis points year on year. This increase in the SG&A employee cost is related to building an international delivery network. And as you know we continue to build critical mass in our network. And we would anticipate that this cost would decline as a percentage of revenue over time. In summary, operating margins for 2007 steadily improved through a combination of several levers that we have talked about throughout the year. We exited the year with a quarterly margin of 25.59%. For those of you who might notice, this is exactly the margin that we had for the full year of last year. And certainly, this is significantly higher than a year ago margin for the same quarter of 24.08%. So we are exiting this quarter with a much higher margin, which will enable us to apply many levers in spite of the wage increase that we will have. Net income, the quarterly net margins have improved both sequentially and year-over-year. Q4 2007 was 22.78% versus Q3 2007 of 32.73% and Q4 2006 of 21.37%. I would like to highlight that over a full year, net margin improved to 22.16% over 21.77% a year ago. We have significant momentum heading into FY 2008, a strong demand environment, our strong book of business, and our significantly improved competitive positioning will continue to drive very strong growth. We'll continue

to focus on all the operational and financial [drivers], and essentially anticipate that even in the face of significant challenges, our strong financial and operational management will enable us to maintain margins in approximately the same ballpark as FY 2007. Thank you. DAVID NELSON: With that, we'll open up the call to questions. OPERATOR: Thank you, very much, sir. At this moment, I would like to hand over the floor to Cynthia to conduct the Q&A session for participants at the international bridge. This will be followed by Q&A session for India participants. Thank you, and over to Cynthia. OPERATOR: Thank you, Pratibha. We will now begin the Q&A session for participants connected to the WebEx international bridge. [OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS] Your first question comes from Joseph Foresi, Janney Montgomery Scott. JOSEPH FORESI, ANALYST, JANNEY MONTGOMERY SCOTT: Hi, guys. And nice work finishing off the year here. My first question is it looks like growth is a little bit slower this quarter in North America, also in application development, maintenance, and financial services. Any color on that? Are you seeing any slowdown on the spend in North America? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: This is Chandra. Thank you for the question. That's not true. Fundamentally, all that's happening is that from a financial services point of view, I want you to look at the annual numbers. In FY06, we had a 41.2% on our total revenues of $2.97 billion. And this year, we've ended the year at 42.2% of $4.3 billion. That's about $1.8 billion. So we've gone from $1.2 billion to $1.8 billion. So the financial services sector has grown 50% year on year. And the fluctuation that we see in the quarter is pretty much related to some large engagements coming to an end and some new ones starting and so on, so forth. It is not in lieu with any slowdown. Our large financial services clients in North America are growing. And the traction is good. Then coming to the North America per se, by and large, the North American market is strong for us. And all of our existing clients

are buying new services from us. And we are also having an excellent client acquisition going. The only thing I would say is that since most of our large clients are North America based, any of the movement of work towards offshore to India or elsewhere is predominantly happening from the North American clients. I would like to even say that even though you don't see specific movement of offshore towards India this quarter, that does not mean that some clients are not moved. What has happened is that some of the North American clients have moved work offshore. And some [of that is], we have moved, work onsite primarily because we are taking on transition [inaudible] engagements. But the momentum is good. JOSEPH FORESI: Sure. Thanks. And my second question here is sort of around headcount. Any initial headcount guidance for fiscal '08? And how are you seeing the labor environment? UNIDENTIFIED COMPANY REPRESENTATIVE: [Inaudible-highly accented language] the [campus] for this year, we are [inaudible]. And the campus offers which we made last year will be joining us in June. Overall, last year, we added totally about 32,000 people, just about 32,000 people, of which about 18% was outside India. JOSEPH FORESI: And so, is there an initial gross hiring guidance for this year, or --? UNIDENTIFIED COMPANY REPRESENTATIVE: No, we -- as a rule we don't give any guidance. So, we're not talking about what the total amount that we will hire this year. JOSEPH FORESI: Okay. Just to -- UNIDENTIFIED COMPANY REPRESENTATIVE: Just to answer your question, sir, it will be in addition to what we announced as 32,000 last year, it'll be more than that for sure. We are currently in the final stages of planning 12,000 offers of that more than 32,000 that's already been made. JOSEPH FORESI: Okay. Great. Thanks, guys. And my last question here is just around the pricing environment. Any color on the pricing environment? And maybe if you can give us just a little bit more color on sort of what you see heading into fiscal '08 overall? Thanks, guys.

UNIDENTIFIED COMPANY REPRESENTATIVE: With regard to pricing, the environment is very encouraging. And the demand is high. And we are continuing to see the kind of pricing that we mentioned in the last quarter. That is about 3% to 5% on existing contracts coming up for renewal. And we're seeing much higher, more in the 5% to 10% range, for new contracts. And that trend continues. JOSEPH FORESI: Okay. And then maybe if you guys could just provide a little bit of guidance, and just how you see the environment shaking out in '08, maybe some areas of growth? Thanks. UNIDENTIFIED COMPANY REPRESENTATIVE: If you're asking about areas of growth, I think we're growing in all markets. And all of our full services are growing. If you really see the services lines in the presentation, what you will find is that all of the services are nicely growing. And whether it's BPO or infrastructure, consulting, even these four services which we introduced in the last 24 months, BPO, global consulting, infrastructure, and assurance, they alone contribute 18% of our revenues. This number used to be 10% last year. So these four services have grown 80%. That's approximately -- work out to something in the range of US$800 million. JOSEPH FORESI: Great. Thanks, guys. OPERATOR: Your next question comes from Trip Chowdhry with Global Equities Research. TRIP CHOWDHRY, ANALYST, GLOBAL EQUITIES RESEARCH: Congratulations on a very good all-around performance. I have a couple of questions. First, is regarding the competitive environment. Are you seeing any visible difference in your competitive engagements in North America, versus Europe and APAC? UNIDENTIFIED COMPANY REPRESENTATIVE: I think each of these markets have different players. So if you're asking about the kind of competition that we face, I can tell you that Europe has European players, who compete with us lot more in Europe, not in the U.S. But overall in terms of deals, it very much depends on the type of the deals rather than the market. If it's more application outsourcing and enterprise application, we face certain type of competition. If it's an infrastructure

deal, the competition is different. If it is a core banking deal, the competition is different. TRIP CHOWDHRY: And also regarding the core banking business, you have your own product. I think it's called Bank One or something like that. UNIDENTIFIED COMPANY REPRESENTATIVE: It's called BANCS, yes. TRIP CHOWDHRY: I was wondering, is that product competing, say, with i-Flex or Finacle? And do you have any specific goals in terms of how you are going to go to market across the globe? And lastly, how do you price it versus, say, something which is a licensed software company? UNIDENTIFIED COMPANY REPRESENTATIVE: The financial services product is pretty important business for TCS. And we have a portfolio of products across the segment, commercial banking, wholesale banking, investment banking, brokerage, clearing and depositories and wealth management, asset management, etc. And this year, we signed up 51 deals for our financial services products, and it contributes to almost close to $100 million; it's about $98 million -- I'm sorry, $120 million would be the revenue for this fiscal year for the financial services products. And we have set up a separate unit within the company, a separate business unit, which is focusing on the financial services product. And they will be aggressively going to the market. But in terms of how we recognize revenues, I think we consider -- we do percentage-of-completion method for both license and [inaudible-highly accented language] put together. OPERATOR: [OPERATOR INSTRUCIONS] Your next question comes from Moshe Katri of Cowen and Company. MOSHE KATRI, ANALYST, COWEN AND COMPANY: Thanks. Nice quarter. Looking into fiscal '08, and I know that you don't provide guidance, but maybe you can talk about your comfort levels in terms of being able to maintain your current EBIT margin. That's number one. And then also in that respect, can you talk a bit about the expected increases in comp during fiscal '08 as well? Thanks. UNIDENTIFIED COMPANY REPRESENTATIVE: Can you repeat that Moshe? That question, we couldn't hear that very well. MOSHE KATRI: Sorry. Talk a bit about your comfort in terms of your ability

to maintain your EBIT margins, i.e. your operating margins, in fiscal '08. And then also in that respect, maybe you can talk about the different levers in the model. And then maybe you can talk a bit about the expected increase in compensation in fiscal '08, especially for [Freshers] and then in general. Thanks. UNIDENTIFIED COMPANY REPRESENTATIVE: Okay. The first thing is we are entering FY08 with a much better margin in Q4 of FY07. So that means, that we can certainly take some amount of wage increase without really affecting the margin, or which will bring us to the margin. And the additional one, we have --sometimes, what we are doing at this time is a few things. One is, we have begun a number of initiatives overseas -- whether it is in terms of the centers in various -- the global network delivery management, or in terms of the subsidiaries and so on. Many of them have started producing [inaudible]. And that'll be one lever which we will crank a little more, because the benefit in terms of their performance is definitely going to be a reflection as far as FY08 is concerned. The second one, at the beginning of this year, we had said that we would move towards more work being shifted offshore to India. And as you can see, we have shifted close to 3.1% to offshore to India. That's another lever that we'll continue. We believe we still have some way to go as far as that lever is concerned. Third, Chandra has already talked about pricing. And the pricing situation is not any different from what we have been articulating in the last couple of quarters, which is the new contracts coming in at a certain higher level as well as old contracts being renegotiated. And some of the contracts, although we have renegotiated, their effective start date for us in the renegotiated terms is really starting from April of this year. And in some cases, it's July of this year and so on. So that lever is certainly there. We began the

year with an effective thing to control the SG&A cost, and that would still continue. We believe that our increased base offers us more possibility for leveraging those. So, there are a number of things that we have put together as we developed the plan, whether it is in terms of pricing, whether it is in terms of productivity improvement, whether it is in terms of getting the fuller benefit as a result of many of these major initiatives that we have started a year back, and whether it is in terms of cost control and so on that we are bringing it. So the impact of rate increase, we expect, is going to be very similar to the impact that we had last year, because the Indian salary, essentially, we are expecting it to grow by 12% to 15%. As far as the overseas is concerned, it is going to be between 3% and 5%. And it is exactly the same as last year. So the impact is going to be more or less the same. And we have worked up this kind of a detailed plan to meet that impact. And that's what gives us confidence that we should be able to meet the goal. There is one additional thing that we have done. And that is on the foreign exchange management. Essentially, we had put together a strategy earlier of ensuring that we are able to protect our realization at a certain rate. And so, we have gone in for forward options and so on. We had budgeted certain costs in terms of premiums when it comes to options. And I think that strategy seems to work extremely well in the volatile kind of situations. And with that, I think that strategy is also something that we will continue to practice. And overall, these are the things that give us confidence that we should be able to maintain the market. OPERATOR: Your next question comes from Julio Quinteros with Goldman Sachs. JULIO QUINTEROS, ANALYST, GOLDMAN SACHS: Thanks. This question is actually for Mah. Can you go through

the other drivers for margins, though, as you look at fiscal year 2008? I didn't hear you mention some of the large clients. And then also the impact of recent acquisitions, how do we think about those impacting fiscal year 2008? SETURAMAN MAHALINGAM: As far as the large accounts are concerned, they are in a major sense the negative impact if at all, are behind us -- where we had to go ahead and start something and so on. And everything that we are doing at this moment in time, maybe in the initial stages that could be a certain increase in onsite, because we are essentially going through a process of knowledge transition in many of those kinds of activities. And then the real benefit in terms of offshore push happens a little later. But, so long as we can have a certain number of large clients, and it doesn't really expand, the hockey stick effect, we will be in a position to handle extremely well. And we have learned that. And we have been practicing that. So, I really don't see very much later on. And Chandra can elaborate on that. And the other one, in terms of acquisitions. Full text: Presentation OPERATOR: Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to the TCS earnings conference call. Please note that for the duration of this presentation, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode and this conference is being recorded. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions. (Operator Instructions). I would now like to turn the conference over to Mr. Kedar Shirali, Director of Investor Relations at TCS. Thank you and over to you, Mr. Shirali. KEDAR SHIRALI, DIRECTOR, IR, TATA CONSULTANCY SERVICES LIMITED: Thank you, Rochelle. Good evening and welcome, everyone. Thank you for joining us today to discuss TCS's financial results for the fourth quarter and full year that ended March 31, 2011. This call is being webcast through our website and an archive including the transcripts will be available on the site for the duration of the quarter. The financial statements, results presentation, and press releases are also available on our website. Our leadership team is present on this call to discuss our results. We have with us today Mr. N. Chandrasekaran, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director. N. CHANDRASEKARAN, CEO, MANAGING DIRECTOR, TATA CONSULTANCY SERVICES LIMITED: Hello, everyone. KEDAR SHIRALI: Mr. S. Mahalingam, Chief Financial Officer and Executive Director. S. MAHALINGAM, CFO, EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR, TATA CONSULTANCY SERVICES LIMITED: Good morning, good afternoon, good evening. KEDAR SHIRALI: Mr. Phiroz Vandrevala, Head of Global Corporate Affairs and Executive Director. PHIROZ VANDREVALA, HEAD OF GLOBAL CORPORATE AFFAIRS, EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR, TATA CONSULTANCY SERVICES LIMITED: Hi, everyone. KEDAR SHIRALI: And Mr. Ajoy Mukherjee, Head of Global Human Resources. AJOY MUKHERJEE, HEAD OF GLOBAL HUMAN RESOURCES, TATA CONSULTANCY SERVICES LIMITED: Hello, everyone. KEDAR SHIRALI: Chandra and Mahal will give us a brief overview of the Company's performance followed by the Q and A session. As you are aware we do not provide specific revenue and earnings guidance. Anything said on this call which reflects our outlook for the future or which can be construed as a forward-looking statement, must be

reviewed in conjunction with the risks that the Company faces. We have outlined these risks in the second slide of the results presentation emailed to you and also made available on our website. With that I'd like to turn the call over to Chandra to begin the proceedings. N. CHANDRASEKARAN: Hello, everyone. Thank you, Kedar. I am very happy to address all of you today. We have had another excellent quarter, and a great year. In terms of growth we have delivered 5.1% growth, but if you look at the international revenues alone it's about 5.5%. So the volume also is much greater than the 2.92% reported, it's around the 3.3% if you look at the international volumes alone. The India market has grown 1%. In terms of the different segments and geographies and services it is again a well-rounded performance. The noteworthy points are we are seeing signs of recovery in Continental Europe. Continental Europe delivered close to 12% growth on a sequential basis, and on a constant currency basis more than 7% growth. And Asia Pacific once again delivered an exceptional growth at close to 10%, and the US continues to be good growing about 4.8% on a Q-on-Q basis. From an industry perspective, banking and financial services continues to do well, but a number of other sectors have delivered upper single-digit growth, and a couple of them have even shown double-digit growth. We have delivered double-digit growth in Hi-Tech and Travel and Hospitality and in Energy and Utilities in these three segments. And then Manufacturing has delivered over 9% growth and Retail and Distribution 7% growth, and BFSI under 4% growth. So there has been a significant growth across verticals. And Telecom has declined, but we are seeing signs of recovery. It will continue to grow from here, but nevertheless it will always be in the near term below the company average growth rate. Coming to the services the most significant thing to notice is a significant uptick that we have had in the Enterprise Solutions space, which kind of indicates the growth in the discretionary spend

and the projects coming thereof. And we have had a double-digit growth on a sequential basis in the Enterprise Solutions. From a customer metrics point of view the -- across the customer revenue bands, if we look at the pyramid it has been excellent client additions whether it's the $1m bracket or a $5m bracket or a $10m bracket or a $20m bracket and so on so forth. It has been very nice to see that there is significant number of additions at the bottom end of that, the customer revenue band pyramid. Then, in terms of the operational metrics, we have had a slight drop in utilization, in fact more than 100 basis point drop, 130 basis point drop in utilization. And that is due to the large number of trainees coming into the system and also Q4 being a seasonally weak quarter. But having said that, we have been able to maintain margin in spite of the drop in utilization at the 28.02% at the EBIT level. Overall, looking forward the deal pipeline is very robust. I would say that the total number of deals that we are chasing the total volume of the deals that we are chasing and the qualified pipeline that we have all of them are much better than the same time last year. And they have been getting incrementally better quarter after quarter. We have had a pricing uptick of 80 basis points this quarter, which is in line with some of our predictions earlier. We have had a pricing uptick in Q3 of 118 basis points and we have followed it up this quarter. Going forward we continue to expect some pricing improvement in the next fiscal year, because the customers by and large are not only focused on cost, they are increasingly focusing on value. And, which drive a significant number of projects due to discretionary spend in the coming year. And also new technology adoption whether it is mobility, whether it is cloud, whether it is social media or analytics, those things will come into play. So we see a

volume-led growth, but there will be some pricing improvement that's what we see. And we are not seeing any specific issues in any of the markets or the industries that we operate in. Those are my initial comments, and I'll pass it onto to Mahal to give you some more color, then we'll be happy to take questions. S. MAHALINGAM: Thank you, Chandra, and you have already seen the -- you have noted the improvement in the revenue sales sequential quarter on quarter as well as year on year, both in rupee terms and dollar terms. Let me just give you the addition factors, for instance on the revenue analytics we had a volume growth of 2.9% and a constant currency pricing improvement of 0.8%. Currency had a positive impact of 1.3% and onsite shift contributed 2.1%. Adding these up you get that 5.1% INR revenue growth, sequential revenue growth for the quarter. For the full year we have had a growth of 24.3% year on year, and I would like to emphasize that in constant currency basis it has been 28.5%. And giving you details in terms of revenue analytics for annual, volume growth was 29.65%, exchange was a minus 4.2%, pricing was a minus 0.3% and effort mix minus 0.85%, so totally 24.3%. As far as the operating margin is concerned we had a 58 basis point benefit from currency in Q4, and this gave us the -- helped us to mitigate the negative impact of onsite shift and higher SG&A, so our operating margin remained flat around -- at 28.02%. For the full year, despite adverse currency movement, our EBIT margin expanded by 134 basis points to 27.8%. There was a 215 basis points negative impact from currency, but this was offset by a 252 basis point gain from SG&A efficiencies, 34 -- 39 basis point gain from offshore shift and 58 basis points from productivity improvements. And adding all these four figures you get a full year of 134 basis point margin improve -- expansion on an annual basis. On the side of net income we

have an effective tax rate in Q4 of 20.8%, and this was offset by the higher other income, so the net income margin came down by just 47 basis points to 23.7%. For the whole year the EBIT margin expansion of higher other income led to 33 basis point year-on-year expansion of our net income margin to 23.3% despite a higher effective tax rate of 19.4% this year compared to 14.9% in FY10. Earnings per share in FY11 was INR44.36 which is a 26% year-on-year growth. In dollar terms EPS was $0.97, which is 31.1% higher than the previous year. We have also announced a final divided of INR8 bringing the total for the year as INR14, which works out to a payout ratio of [36.7%]. Our DSOs stayed flat at 80, and invested funds stood at INR93.6b. So in conclusion, despite all kinds of economic uncertainties from threats of double-dip recession in the US to sovereign defaults in Europe, FY2011 turned out to be a year of strong demand. And we are very happy on how we foresaw this and created sufficient capacity in advance, which helped us exploit this demand surge. Another source of much satisfaction to us is that the cost management exercise we started during the downturn evolved into something much more substantive over the year. On the one hand, we were able to optimize and stabilize our cost structures to enhance operational efficiency, and to meet the organizations' strategic imperatives. On the other hand, we were able to ensure sustainability by building an institutional framework for decentralizing the control process. This is what helped us expand our operating margin, and hold it at a very narrow band through the year despite all the heavy headwinds. All in all, we began this -- we begin the new fiscal year from a comfortable stance. With good demand and a sustainable margin structure, we are confident [of having] another year of profitable growth. With that, we can open the lines for questions. Questions and Answers OPERATOR: Thank you very much. (Operator Instructions). The first question is from the

line of Moshe Katri of Cowen and Company. Please go ahead. MOSHE KATRI, ANALYST, COWEN & COMPANY: Thanks. Chandra, I'm looking at some of the revenue metrics, it seems that the UK was a bit weak for the quarter, the infrastructure also a bit weak for the quarter. Maybe you can comment on that. And then how should we think about margins considering the fact that we are looking at record, still record utilization rate levels, keeping in mind that utilization rates will decline in the next few quarters and then you do have some headwinds coming in from FX and wage inflation? Thanks. N. CHANDRASEKARAN: We think from the revenue contribution point of a view, yes, it has been a soft quarter for the UK this quarter and we think it will get better going forward. There is nothing structurally wrong. There are no client specific issues as far as the UK is concerned. So I think that it is just a one-off from a demand point of view. It will continue to get better from here, and it will do well in FY11/12. From an infrastructure solutions point of view, this has been one of the fastest growing services for us and it will continue to be so. We have signed a number of deals, very large deals, transformational deals and we are in the process of executing them. In India, our revenues is down, there is a portion of infrastructure revenues that are coming from India, and that assignment got over last quarter, and that has resulted in a dip this quarter. But otherwise infrastructure services is doing extremely well both in terms of pipeline, the order book the -- currently what we are transitioning and executing it's doing very, very well so there is no cause for concern. And from the point of view of margins I think the first thing I would like to highlight is the margins that we are [exiting] is one of the best ever we have done. On a quarterly basis it's almost at our all-time high that 28.02%. If you

look at the annual basis, again this is the best margin that we have exited in a financial year. So there has been a lot of discipline in the way we have approached the business. We have overcome wage increases, promotion cost increases, currency headwinds all those things we have very definitely handled all through the year. And you are absolutely right, there are headwinds coming in terms of wage increase and we have given a substantial wage increase 12% to 14%. And there will be promotion costs and there will be possible currency-related challenges. I think from a lever perspective, utilization we used to say we are comfortable at 78% 80% at utilization for -- excluding trainees. That will no longer be the case. I think we are pretty comfortable operating between 82% and 84%, and that's the level at which we'll operate. So I don't see a reason for a significant drop in utilization at the excluding trainee level. Including trainee level will depend on the inflow. Already we have come down this quarter, next quarter there will not be much of trainee additions, trainee additions will come in the second quarter. So I expect in Q1 the utilization to go up from here. So utilization will be a lever that we will definitely deploy. And growth, growth is very, very critical. I think if growth comes that will definitely help. And we are going to work on pricing. Having said that I don't want to indicate that there will be a significant increase in pricing, but the demand environment currently indicates there will be a pricing increase. And so we are going to work on that. So there will be a growth lever, there will be a utilization lever and there will be a pricing lever. And of course we will continue to look at optimizing costs on SG&A. It has gone up slightly this quarter. We are investing in huge new infrastructures. But we'll continue to look at that, and then try to optimize. Those will be my comments on margin. MOSHE KATRI: Thanks for the

color. OPERATOR: Thank you, Mr. Katri. Our next question is from the line of Balaji Prasad of Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead. BALAJI PRASAD, ANALYST, GOLDMAN SACHS: Thank you. Congratulations on your continuing great trend I have two questions, firstly with two of your large Indian peers being in the middle of management changes, business restructuring how does this alter the competitive landscape in your favor? Are you seeing them where you would normally have? Are you not seeing them in RFPs or bidding process where you'd normally have seen them? Are you getting any market share [are you]? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: No, I don't think that I will comment on that. I don't think there is a competitive advantage or anything of that kind. I think from our point of view I would say that we have a structure that we put in place, and actually that's firing all cylinders. That's why you are seeing a well-rounded growth across verticals and across markets. And we have got a good platform. Our full services strategy is really getting traction. So there is good demand environment. We are firing all cylinders, but I'm not looking at this as something that will not perhaps --- well, not that will happen to us in a quarter or two, because of any particular situation elsewhere. BALAJI PRASAD: Okay, great. So if we understand correctly it's not a market share that you're grabbing elsewhere but the general burgeoning demand environment. N. CHANDRASEKARAN: There will be -- I think there will always be a combination, okay, but the point is that we are on a path which we have put in place a couple of years ago and we are going on the path and we are seeing a lot of traction. The teams are all delivering results, and we are seeing opportunities and we want to increase the velocity and fire on all cylinders, as simple as that. BALAJI PRASAD: Okay, thank you. My second question is could you just give some clarity on pricing, I just also wanted to get your views on how much

of this was related to COLA adjustment or competitive differentiation, or just a resurgent demand scenario. N. CHANDRASEKARAN: I really think -- I think the combination, and COLA will always be a clear factor and when we have low demand COLA doesn't hold an argument, when we have demand, COLA has an argument. And also the differentiation in the type of engagements you do has an argument. And today's costs in a demand environment has an argument. So I definitely see enough reasons for a pricing uptick. But I would caution anyone in factoring in a pricing growth immediately in the subsequent quarters. We have had two quarters where there is a gradual increase. And it'll take some more time but we are going to be trying to see what happens. BALAJI PRASAD: Fair enough. That's helpful. Thank you and good luck to the team. OPERATOR: Thank you Mr. Prasad. Our next question is from the line of Diviya Nagarajan of UBS. Please go ahead. DIVIYA NAGARAJAN, ANALYST, UBS: Hi, congrats on the quarter. Just a couple of questions, I heard your comments on CNBC and if I'm not mistaken you guided for about a 60,000 headcount addition this year, is that correct? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: Yes, from a total headcount addition we'll get 60,000. DIVIYA NAGARAJAN: I'm just trying to reconcile that with then the statements of growth and outlook, because this year you've added almost 70,000 people and -- N. CHANDRASEKARAN: And all those 70,000 odd people are not yet billable. DIVIYA NAGARAJAN: Right, right. N. CHANDRASEKARAN: So all of them -- many of them are on the bench. DIVIYA NAGARAJAN: Got that. But even if I assume some utilization improvement we are probably looking at volume growth being in the high teens or maybe close to around 19%, 20%. Is that a fair assumption to make, or do you think that as the year progresses you could actually look at hiring more people if needed? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: Diviya, we don't give guidance so we can't tell you clearly how much will be the growth, but all we can

say is that the pipeline, the qualified pipeline today is better than last year and we have hired 70,000 as a post-year target of 50,000 so those people are on the bench and going through training and we will look to increase utilization. And we have already made 35,000 offers in the colleges. We expect at least 23,000 people coming from the 35,000 hires we've made an offer to. Then remaining will be lateral hires through the year. But currently our estimate is 60,000 people. DIVIYA NAGARAJAN: Got that, got that. N. CHANDRASEKARAN: And then we will be focusing on non-linear as well, that's a priority. Although it will not show significant revenue numbers this year, we are definitely giving it a top priority. DIVIYA NAGARAJAN: Right, right. Could you give us also a sense of within your BFSI sector is there any divergence in trends between what you've observed in the banking capital markets and on the insurance side? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: Can you repeat the question, Diviya? DIVIYA NAGARAJAN: Within the banking financial services and insurance vertical is there any divergence in growth trends this quarter for capital markets vis-a-vis the other parts of the business, maybe insurance or other parts of the vertical? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: In Q4 insurance grew less than the BFSI. DIVIYA NAGARAJAN: Right, got that. And lastly, -- just on the promotion costs, will the promotion costs be over and above the rate hikes that you have guided for, and this year what will be the impact of that on margins? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: No, that is 12% to 14% what I have said that includes the promotion costs element. DIVIYA NAGARAJAN: Got that. Thanks and all the best for the next year, thanks. N. CHANDRASEKARAN: Thank you. OPERATOR: Thank you, Miss Nagarajan. Our next question is from the line of Viju George of JP Morgan. Please go ahead. VIJU GEORGE, ANALYST, JPMORGAN: Yes, hi. Congratulations to the management team on yet another fine quarter. My question relates to the comment made by Chandra earlier that utilization and in a steady state ex-trainees can now be

consistently at between the 82% to 84%. That's quite interesting because people thought that running at more than 80% in subsequent quarters might be a bit difficult. Can you just take us through how that has changed in the past and why you think this might be sustainable? Thank you. N. CHANDRASEKARAN: Viju, there are two points. First is that that is the intent, I am not saying that we will always be able to run between 82% and 84%, but goal is to run in that range because we are already close to 200,000 employees, the size has to count. At 200,000 employees if you are at 82% that leaves a lot of room still. That's the basic point. And the fact that we have been able to do 82%, 82.5%, 83.5% during the year gives us the mechanism to be able to achieve that. In fact, if you look at last year, all through from Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, we have always been between 82% and 84%. We started the year at 82.8% then we crossed 83% to go to 83.8%, 82.6%, 83.8%, 83.8% and 82.4%. So that's a pretty credible range that we have been able to manage. So if you are going to add people more the expectation is that we should try and do that. VIJU GEORGE: Sure, thank you, all the best. OPERATOR: Thank you, Mr. George. Our next question is from the line of Srivatsan Ramachandran from Spark Capital. Please go ahead. SRIVATSAN RAMACHANDRAN, ANALYST, SPARK CAPITAL: Yes, hi. I just wondered if you could update the [saleable] hedge book currently stands at around [$0.9b] I just wanted to know the effective rates you run, what kind of tenure those hedge book would be. N. CHANDRASEKARAN: These are all for short term of about three months or so, and the effective rate is some -- around INR45. SRIVATSAN RAMACHANDRAN: INR45, sure. My next question is on the BPO business, just wanted to get an update on--- you set initially about a target of $3b kind of number 2015/16 just wanted to know how

was it doing and what's happening in the (inaudible). Just given that now we've taken a couple of clients on the new platform what kind of traction, are we on track to maybe take it forward to some other countries out of UK. N. CHANDRASEKARAN: Yes, the BPO business is doing well. Already we are almost $1b, a little less than $1b on an annual basis. And so we are on a growth trajectory in BPO. And on an FY11 basis it is maintaining its share more or less in the overall revenue of TCS. So BPO business is doing well. From a [deliverance] point of view, Phiroz, can you add? PHIROZ VANDREVALA: Basically we are on track, we've had a good year, we've had a year as per planned. The traction in the UK market has been significantly high and we are quite confident of growth in the period coming ahead. In respect of going to other markets, the current thinking is to actually leverage the bench at home rather than repeat the general model of trying in-source large numbers of people. But we are keeping eyes and ears open, and some opportunities, especially in Europe, are presenting themselves and we are in the process of evaluating whether we should do a platform positioning or go back and see whether we want to (inaudible) SRIVATSAN RAMACHANDRAN: Thank you. Thanks a lot. OPERATOR: Thank you, Mr. Ramachandran. Our next question is from the line of Sandeep Shah of RBS. Please go ahead. SANDEEP SHAH, ANALYST, RBS: Yes, congrats on a good quarter. Just in terms of pricing we've talk about 80 bps constant currency pricing improvement, so is it largely coming through service and exchange because this time we had discretionary services also growing faster or is it also some bit of a COLA adjustment reflected in this? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: I think it is a combination. Service mix certainly has played a role. And also some of the contracts that we renewed are getting into effect. SANDEEP SHAH: Okay. And, Chandra, you also spoke about most of the margin headwinds

and the tailwinds and your comments have also been positive in terms of the growth going forward. So in that scenario this high margin with this like 28% on an EBIT level you expect on the constant currency likely to be maintained? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: We don't give guidance, but our intent is to grow the business with a margin focus. SANDEEP SHAH: Okay. S. MAHALINGAM: You know, Sandeep, we have been talking about 27% and so on. This year, we obviously have done exceedingly well, and I have also said we will have an ideal margin structure, so I think we will leave it at that. N. CHANDRASEKARAN: Then and you know you should expect with the kind of headwinds we have and the clients in Q1, but then you should also know that we are going to be driving the business with a clear focus on profits as well. SANDEEP SHAH: Okay. And sir, on CNBC you also talked about some bit of organizational change which can allow a faster decision making. Can you throw some more light, exactly what was the focus? Is it to become more aggressive within the market or is there any change in the demand trends? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: I did not speak anything about organizational change. Yesterday when I was in a function there was a question for which I answered that the organizational structure we put in place two years ago has really delivered results for us, it has brought in agility, it has brought in the well-rounded growth across industries and markets. And, as organizations evolve there will always be incremental changes. That was a broad comment, but I did not make any specific comment on a change. SANDEEP SHAH: Okay. Thanks, and all the best. OPERATOR: Thank you Mr. Shah. Our next question is from the line of Nitin Mohta of Macquarie. Please go ahead. NITIN MOHTA, ANALYST, MACQUARIE: -- taking my question. Chandra, this is more regarding the comment you made about a couple of quarters ago about 10% incremental revenues coming from cloud services. You also launched the SME

product. I wanted to understand from a three-year perspective if you can tell us how you plan to scale this product up and what are your thoughts on that. N. CHANDRASEKARAN: We said that the 10% of our incremental revenues will come from non-linear initiatives from Q4 of FY12, and we are sticking to that. And we have a multi-dimensional strategy for non-linear growth. We are driving the products business, and the second one is the BPO cloud, process cloud we call it or BPO platforms. The third one is iON. All the three are significant areas of focus for TCS, especially this fiscal year. And we definitely want to deliver that 10% of incremental revenues. But actually the importance there is not whether it is 10% or 8% or 15%. The importance there is to put them on a trajectory where from there they will grow at a faster rate than the rest of the company for a sustainable period of time, and that's the focus and that's what we intend to achieve. And I can't really tell you how much it will be three years from now. I hope it is very material. We are working on (inaudible) numbers, and we are putting significant effort. And the incremental revenues from the non-linear business has to be material when you look at a three-year horizon. NITIN MOHTA: Sure thanks. In terms of any feedback from clients in early stages about these initiatives, that would be very helpful. N. CHANDRASEKARAN: Currently it's all positive, a lot of interest, lots of positive, but I would like proof points. I would like really to see a significant number of clients, for example in iON we want to see 1,000 clients, operating extremely -- and express extreme level of satisfaction on everything about iON. And also we want to see the right financial model which we originally constructed being proven. And I hope that we can share some specific data at the end of the FY '11/'12 fiscal. NITIN MOHTA: Sure, thank you. OPERATOR: Thank you, Mr. Mohta. Our next question is from

the line of Mitali Ghosh of Bank of America Merrill Lynch. MITALI GHOSH, MERRILL LYNCH - ANALYST, BANK OF AMERICA: Yes, thanks and congratulations to the team. First, I just wanted to understand that when you went into the quarter were you expecting the kind of volume growth that you saw in this quarter, or was it perhaps a little softer than what you expected? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: I think, at the beginning of the quarter, I think the volume growth we always expected between 3% to 4%. And the international business has delivered that. It's just that the Indian business has gone down, or has been very, very marginal this quarter and to some extent that has brought the volume numbers below 3%. Otherwise 3% to 4% was a good growth for this quarter. And I think we've done very well on that basis with the way we've been able to manage margins. And if you see the line items, we've made improvements in gross margins. And that's very credible. MITALI GHOSH: Right. So have there been any -- were there any delays in ramp up in the international side, and have all those projects started now, so should one expect that any delays that you saw are clearly behind us now? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: I don't want to say delays. What I want to say is that all the discretionary projects that get finalized and the spend approved don't start on January 1. That's the nature of Q4, and that's why many times Q4 is referred to as seasonally weak quarter because things take a while. In some markets, it's January 10, in some markets, it's January end, those kind of things happen in this quarter. But I'm not saying there is any delay, postponement, a deliberate postponement of projects because of a particular situation in any client or in a market. MITALI GHOSH: Okay. Secondly, just on the pricing, wanted to understand that the number you gave us was a blended pricing number, 80 basis points. Any sense on how that's moved onsite and offshore, because onsite has gone

up this time, so I'm just trying to understand how much of it is due to mix and how much of it is pure pricing. N. CHANDRASEKARAN: Mitali, we never share that, right. UNIDENTIFIED COMPANY REPRESENTATIVE: (technical difficulty) it's because of onsite shift. We've taken out the onsite shift, and it's after stripping onsite shift. MITALI GHOSH: Okay. This is pure pricing. UNIDENTIFIED COMPANY REPRESENTATIVE: Yes, pure pricing. MITALI GHOSH: Okay, sure. Thanks, that's helpful. And just in terms of the outlook, I had two questions. One is if you could give some color around the large deals that you have signed this quarter and the kind of pipeline you have. And secondly on the banking, BFSI vertical, last year has been quite a phenomenal year for spending by BFSI. So what you feel are the trends this year and whether that will grow at above Company average. N. CHANDRASEKARAN: You see there are a couple of comments I want to make. In terms of deals, we signed several large deals during the quarter and one of which is in banking and financial services. The remaining came across multiple verticals, retail, financial services, manufacturing, high tech industries -- two in manufacturing, and then one public services. So there are seven large deals we signed. And again they came across markets, US dominated with four deals, and three other deals came, one in each of the different markets. And in terms of the pipeline that we are having, as I said, the total pipeline and the qualified pipeline that we chase today is definitely much better than what we had last year and also what we have seen every quarter. So it's getting better and better. We are chasing more than 20 deals which are very material in terms of size, quite large in size. And they are full services deals. They come across verticals and across markets, both on the efficiency side and also on the discretionary spend side. What was the second question you had? MITALI GHOSH: On BFSI, whether it will grow at about -- N. CHANDRASEKARAN: Mitali,

the point I want to make is that if you take US and BFS as two distinct things where we have a significant presence, one from a geography perspective, one from a industry perspective, both are growing. We are significantly present, but they are nowhere near saturation. They have a lot of upside and a lot of headroom to grow for us. The second point I make is that, having said that, the dependency on them are not increasing because the rest of the business, whether it's from a market perspective or from a industry perspective, is growing, and we are putting tremendous emphasis and focus on the other markets and other industries. So they will continue to grow, but they will not become like -- they will not make us more dependent on them than ever before or anything like that. I hope I'm able to give you what you wanted. MITALI GHOSH: Right. No, I think that's very helpful. And, finally, if I can just ask two quick questions. One is, I didn't catch the hiring number correctly, was it 50,000, 5 - 0 or 60,000? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: 6 - 0. MITALI GHOSH: 6 - 0 okay. And just another question on the fresher to lateral hiring mix, what it was last year and what you're perhaps targeting this year. N. CHANDRASEKARAN: Last year? AJOY MUKHERJEE: Last year we have done, it's around -- in India if I look at, because that's where we try to look at, it's about 56 to 44 -- 55/45, 56/44 was the mix that we had. And this year, going forward, I think what we are planning is more closer towards 50/50 at this point in time. MITALI GHOSH: Okay. The 56 was lateral last year? AJOY MUKHERJEE: Right. MITALI GHOSH: Okay, thank you and wish you the best. OPERATOR: Thank you, Ms. Ghosh. Our next question is from Anthony Miller of TechMarketView. Please go ahead. ANTHONY MILLER, ANALYST, TECHMARKETVIEW: Yes, gentlemen, can I just come back to the organization issue again. You're now -- well, you probably are at 200,000 employees.

And it's very possible that this time next year we'll be talking about a quarter of a million employees. And in maybe three or four year's time, if we can sustain these growth rates, it's going to be more than half a million or more like half a million. So you talk about incremental changes to your organization, but at what point, at what number of employees do you think the incremental won't be enough and you'll have to undertake another, fairly significant reorganization. And what sort of shape do you think that might take? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: I think there's no point in discussing it in great detail here, but I'll tell you this. We put in a structure two years ago where we had 23 units. And they all have strong leadership teams and each one of them are capable of managing a billion dollar business. So we have a very strong leadership team in place. And whether we alter it, whether we support it with more bandwidth, etc., is something that we will constantly look at. There is no point in -- with a theory, because to be very frank and honest when we were 50,000 people we didn't know how we will manage 100,000 people company from -- structurally. When we were 100,000 people, we had no clue how we will manage a 200,000 people company. And it's just that we have constantly looked at it and we have done the right thing. And we have a structure where we have highly [on-board] teams and the government, the mechanisms, the controls in place. And we are going ahead with it and we will do the right thing. ANTHONY MILLER: Okay, thank you very much. OPERATOR: Thank you, Mr. Miller. Our next question is from the line of Rishi Maheshwari of Enam AMC. Please go ahead. RISHI MAHESHWARI, ANALYST, ENAM AMC: Thanks and congratulations to the management for a good deal -- a good score this time. I was just seeking a little more explanation on the utilization remark that you made. You explained this earlier, but a

little more commentary on that will be helpful. Is it correct to assume that at now close to about 200,000 people, we should view the bench as an absolute number than utilization percentage as we've been used to seeing it also? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: We look at it both ways. Internally, we look at it both ways. RISHI MAHESHWARI: But, Chandra, is it now more meaningful that -- probably a 20,000, 25,000 bench is more meaningful than having to see about 15% or 20% bench on the total number? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: See, you can definitely take that view, except that you also have to keep the growth environment in mind. RISHI MAHESHWARI: So therefore two, three years down the line can we also expect that utilization can go up to 87%, 88%? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: It's very hypothetical. Why don't we leave it for at least for at least a couple of years? RISHI MAHESHWARI: Sure, sure. And anything on your acquisition strategy that you'd like to highlight upon? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: No, I think, except that we will do things sensibly. If there is an opportunity for us to bring a new strategic capability, in terms of a business model in terms of a industry or in terms of a geography, we will do that, but we will be very sensible about it. And we won't do anything for the sake of revenues. RISHI MAHESHWARI: Sure. Okay, thanks. Congratulations once again. OPERATOR: Thank you, Mr. Maheshwari. Our next question is from the line of Nitin Padmanabhan of IndiaBulls Securities. Please go ahead. NITIN PADMANABHAN, ANALYST, INDIABULLS SECURITIES: Yes hi. Thank you for taking my questions. Congrats on a great quarter. You had -- were giving a 12% to 14% salary hike this -- for the next fiscal. Do you find that the overall job market for next year seems -- is actually tighter than what we saw in the previous year, that is FY '11? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: From a job market point of view and the kind of talent that we need, we are able to get it from the market. But

is it getting tighter? Probably yes. NITIN PADMANABHAN: So I -- you were mentioning about 343 colleges that we've picked up fresher from. N. CHANDRASEKARAN: Right. NITIN PADMANABHAN: So is it that we are possibly -- the change in mix to 50/50, has it got something to do with the overall pool available being a little lower? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: See, I think, Nitin, the way to look at it is this. At the beginning of a year we do a plan in terms of how many people we're going to hire. And based on which we decide, ideally we would like to get 60% of the people from colleges and 40% laterals. Some years it will be 65%/35% divide, some years it will be 55%/45%. It depends on the current employee pyramid structure we have and we decide that. But what happens is that in a year if the growth momentum picks up, then within the year all the extra hiring you do we have to go lateral. You see last year we went a significant amount of lateral hires because the 20,000 people is an upward revision that came during the year. So if you see a demand environment changing in a positive direction during the year, I think you will end up hiring more laterals in addition to, obviously, the skill sets, the types of engagements, etc. NITIN PADMANABHAN: Sure, sure. Just one more, you were mentioning that we're chasing 20 deals which are very material in terms of size. Have the [TCs] of the deals that we've been chasing increased in size versus last year, what we would have seen at the same time last year? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: I think that's not a factor of last year into this year, that's a factor of the Company's scale today and the recognition for the Company today that we are invited to larger deals. I don't think that it is -- I just don't want to say that it is because of last year's market situation and this year's market situation. Today we are definitely -- NITIN PADMANABHAN: But

it (multiple speakers) larger than what was seen earlier? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: Yes, could be. Yes. NITIN PADMANABHAN: Sure, fair enough. Thank you so much. OPERATOR: Thank you, Mr. Padmanabhan. Our next question is from the line of Jeff Rossetti of Janney Montgomery Scott. Please go ahead. JEFF ROSSETTI, ANALYST, JANNEY MONTGOMERY SCOTT: Yes. Jeff Rossetti for Joe Foresi. I just wanted to ask if you could talk about your onsite hiring plans and how it differs from last year. Thank you. N. CHANDRASEKARAN: Onsite we will be hiring. And the number of hires that we would have will be very similar to what we have done last year, and the focus would be in US, the focus would be in Latin America and these countries. JEFF ROSSETTI: No specific number that you could provide? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: No, not yet. Not yet. JEFF ROSSETTI: Thank you. OPERATOR: Thank you, Mr. Rossetti. Our next question is from the line of Ankur Rudra of Ambit. Please go ahead. ANKUR RUDRA, ANALYST, AMBIT CAPITAL: Hi, thanks for taking my question. Congrats on a strong quarter. Just one thing on the discretionary spending, you mentioned it's been strong and, obviously, reflected in the Enterprise Solutions being very strong. I wanted to understand, in that context, the weakness in Consulting and also Products. N. CHANDRASEKARAN: I think for Products Q4 is a seasonal issue and we had a great Q3. And you're not going to see a tremendous consistency, but the point is that it has done reasonably well. And we're seeing excellent pipeline. The traction is very, very good. But if you really look at the annual level, from FY '10 to FY '11 the Products business has grown 43% in dollar terms. That is against a 29% dollar term growth for the Company. I think that's pretty significant, and the pipeline is pretty strong and the size of the deals are going up. And we are getting opportunities across our portfolio, whether it's retail banking or investment banking or capital markets, insurance, market infrastructure, global custody. And if you see the research reports, we're

pretty much atop the chart in every analyst's report for our various financial services products. I think that business is on a very, very solid platform for growth. ANKUR RUDRA: Fine. And then just on the Consulting and discretionary spending side, are you seeing specifically those projects lengthening out into larger engagements compared to what you saw in FY '11, earlier part of FY '11. N. CHANDRASEKARAN: If you see the Global Consulting, Global Consulting also, while it has gone down in Q4, on a year on year it has done, on a dollar terms basis, 47%. Yes, it's very small in size, but still 47% growth is very credible. And we are getting lots of opportunities. But we have not -- we are not growing the Consulting business just from a revenue perspective. Our Consulting business is tightly integrated with TCS's core business. And what we really aspire to do is to leverage the top leadership, all the intellectual property we have, the process knowledge we have, and round it up with a strong program management and change management and deliver value to customers. From a financial perspective, there are two or three impacts it will make. Definitely for the work we do in Consulting, the billing rates are significantly higher. The second thing it does, it kind of positions us early in the game in many of the transnational engagements. And we are seeing that and there are enough examples of proof points in (inaudible) but by no means we are in an optimal situation where we would like to be. So it is some more work to do, but it is on the right track and that is our attraction. ANKUR RUDRA: Just one last question, could you comment a bit more on the health of the telecom vertical in terms of demand? Thanks. N. CHANDRASEKARAN: See, the telecom vertical on a year-on-year basis has grown 23%. And it is lower than the Company average of 29%. But 23% for a very weak vertical -- for a vertical where we have had a lot of weakness, is

not bad. So we are expecting the telecom vertical to grow but, at least in the first two quarters, I expect the telecom vertical to grow at a rate lower than the Company average. But I am pretty sure that it's going to deliver quarter-on-quarter growth. ANKUR RUDRA: Any changes to the kind of opportunities you're seeing in telecom which is driving probably this slowdown and then possibly growth towards the end of the year? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: Nothing I can pick up. We keep studying it. Nothing specific that I can pick up as a pattern and tell you. ANKUR RUDRA: All right. Thanks a lot and best wishes. OPERATOR: Thank you, Mr. Rudra. Our next question is from the line of Rachael Stormonth of NelsonHall. Please go ahead. RACHAEL STORMONTH, ANALYST, NELSONHALL: Hi. Congratulations on a sterling quarter to finish off the year. Very impressed by the growth seen in the new service lines and on verticals and US geography. Could you elaborate please on the trends in Latin America this last quarter and really for the year, what you've seen in constant currency year-on-year growth rate this quarter? And can you -- just if you could give us some clarification on the business there, please? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: See, I've said it in the past, whenever we grow in new markets we need to get certain size and -- to deliver consistency in terms of growth rates. From a Latin America point of view, we have attained, overall, a sensible size. We are over $300m in revenue in that market, but we are present in multiple countries. In some countries we have achieved a size and a business mix between annuity revenues and discretionary projects where we can expect to grow consistently. Still there are countries in the region where we are heavily dependent on discretionary projects and so we see volatility in the Latin American revenues. And in this quarter we pretty much had a growth of about 3.5% in constant currency terms in Latin America. RACHAEL STORMONTH: Thank you. And looking ahead will the strategy of Latin

America, will it continue to be as it was or will it be -- since you've made a small acquisition a number of years back, are you looking for any inorganic growth in Latin America. N. CHANDRASEKARAN: No, we're looking at organic growth. I explained in one of the calls earlier, we have some excellent clients in the region who are not only -- there are two types of clients. We are having global customers from the US whom we serve in that market, but more importantly we have developed strong relationship with some of the regional local champions, or national champions as we call it. And we have such clients in Brazil, in Mexico, in Colombia, in other markets, in Chile. And those clients are developing deep relationships and partnerships with us, and we are slowly but steadily growing in those accounts. So our strategy is to grow from here organically. I expect both the revenues and the margins to go up in the region. RACHAEL STORMONTH: Thank you. OPERATOR: Thank you, Ms. Stormonth. Our next question is from the line of Subhashini Gurumurthy of Ambit Capital. Please go ahead. SUBHASHINI GURUMURTHY, ANALYST, AMBIT CAPITAL: Hi. Most of the questions have been answered, but, Chandra, when you mentioned about pricing increase being a margin lever in FY '12, are you seeing it coming from a mix change, or did you mention about like-to-like price increases? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: I'm hoping for like-to-like. I can't commit on it, but I'm hoping for like-to-like. SUBHASHINI GURUMURTHY: Sure. And second, would you like to comment on the decline in the $100m-client base. N. CHANDRASEKARAN: See there are always a few clients who are on the cusp in the $90m to $100m range. So one such client who was marginally ahead, one above $100m, has gone slightly below. And that's not a Q4 impact, that's more a Q1 -- last year Q4 to Q1 there was a decline in the clients. So even though there is an increase in Q4, now on a -- since it is a LTM basis, you are seeing a

decline from nine to eight. Absolutely, there is no cause for concern on any specific clients. The client metrics is pretty good, and it's good to find out that all the four quarters this year we have had an incremental revenue of $100m plus. SUBHASHINI GURUMURTHY: Sure, sure. Thanks a lot. That's all from my side. OPERATOR: Thank you, Ms. Gurumurthy. Our next question is from the line of Dipesh Mehta of SBICAP Securities. Please go ahead. DIPESH MEHTA, ANALYST, SBICAP SECURITIES: In terms of demand, whether we are seeing any divergence in US and Europe and rest of the world. And in general, what kind of demand we are seeing from different geographies. That is the first question. Second about just to understand what kind of growth we expect, because NASSCOM has guided around 16% to 18% for industry. So your comment about where we would be. And last is about client. Your top ten client is showing some kind of relative lower performance compared to Company average. So if any specific comment to make. N. CHANDRASEKARAN: From a market perspective, US is definitely doing better than Europe. And while Europe has picked up momentum, I expect US to grow faster. There are a lot more opportunities. Faster [redemption] cycle, etc. are leading to higher growth in the US. But the other markets which are growing, Asia Pacific is growing almost 10% this quarter. And other markets like Middle East, Africa are growing. And LatAm will grow from here. So that's the color on that. I don't think there should be any concern in terms of any specific client. As I said, on a large base there will always be volatility between our top client, our top five clients, our top ten clients. But in absolute terms, all of them are growing. That's more important. And in terms of the FY '12 growth, see, we don't give guidance, but we have already been ahead of the NASSCOM estimates. DIPESH MEHTA: Okay, thanks. And last is about US, because some of the players have suggested they are seeing some kind

of softness in US. So I just want to understand whether we are seeing the same thing or no? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: We are not seeing any softness. DIPESH MEHTA: Thanks. OPERATOR: Thank you, Mr. Mehta. Our next question is from the line of Ganesh Duwuri of Edelweiss Securities. Please go ahead. KUNAL SANGOI, ANALYST, EDELWEISS SECURITIES: Yes, hi. This is Kunal here. My question is on -- Chandra, you had earlier mentioned that life sciences and healthcare you see particularly good traction. Could you talk about what kind of opportunities are emanating from this particular sector and what would be the service lines that you see here? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: From a life sciences perspective, I think it's full services. We see lot of opportunities in the IT services, good opportunities in BPO. We work with a good number of top ten pharma companies and we work in drug discovery, safety, chemical data, statistical analysis, all kinds of areas we work with them. We are helping them in programs to bring drugs to market faster. We are doing a significant number of engineering services work where we are helping them design products on transplants. And we do -- so engineering services we do a lot of work. We do a lot of KPO work. IT services, we're also doing infrastructure work in terms of consolidation, virtualization etc. Assurance services, pharma companies are leveraging us on a well-rounded basis, and we do a lot of compliance work recently. And there are a lot of regulatory changes coming in the US, ICD-10 and so on and those kind of work is also picking up momentum. KUNAL SANGOI: Right. So by and large maybe over the last two to three quarters would you have seen the size of deals and also the willingness to offshore to Indian players increasing substantially? N. CHANDRASEKARAN: I don't know if there was any problem in willingness to increase to offshore players from our pharma clients, but we have achieved quite a bit of traction, and definitely the KPO work has gained momentum also. KUNAL SANGOI: Sure. Thanks a

lot. OPERATOR: Thank you, Mr. Duwuri. Ladies and gentlemen, due to time constraints, that was the last question. I now hand the conference over to Mr. N. Chandrasekaran to add closing comments. Please go ahead, sir. N. CHANDRASEKARAN: Thank you. I think, in summary, we've had an excellent quarter to round off a good FY '11. And, as we exit, we are coming off the last four quarters where we've had incremental revenues of $100m plus in every quarter. So there is a good growth momentum and our pipelines look healthy and number of deals that we are chasing look good. The customer pyramid in terms of revenues bands looks very good. And in terms of margins, as I said earlier, we are exiting at the best margin levels we have ever exited a financial year. We are conscious of the macro-environment and we are conscious of the headwinds that are in front of us in terms of the wage increases, in terms of the currency, etc. But we are preparing for a good year ahead. You can see it in the number of associates that we have recruited and the guidance we have given for the recruitment next year. Thank you for your support. Have a nice day. OPERATOR: Thank you, Mr. Chandrasekaran, members of the management team and Mr. Shirali. Full text: OPERATOR: Good morning ladies and gentlemen. I am [Mulali] the moderator for this conference. Welcome to the TCS earnings conference call. For the duration of the presentation all participants' lines will be in a listen only mode. After the presentation the question and answer session will be conducted for international participants connected to SingTel. After that, the question and answer session will be conducted for participants in India. I would now like to hand over to the TCS management. Thank you and over to the TCS management. KISHORE BELAI, INVESTOR RELATIONS, TATA CONSULTANCY SERVICES: Thank you [Mulali]. Good morning to everyone and welcome to our second quarter earnings conference call. I am Kishore Belai from the TCS Investor Relations team. I am sure you have all analyzed our results by this time. The results presentation, financial statement and press release have been uploaded on our website. Our leadership team is present on this call to discuss the results with you. Most of you are familiar with them, but nonetheless I would like to introduce them to you. Mr S Ramadorai our CEO and Managing Director. MR S RAMADORAI, CEO AND MANAGING DIRECTOR, TATA CONSULTANCY SERVICES: Good morning. KISHORE BELAI: Mr S Mahalingam, our Chief Financial Officer. MR S MAHALINGAM, CFO, TATA CONSULTANCY SERVICES: Hello. KISHORE BELAI: Mr N Chandrasekaran, Executive Vice President and Head of Global Operations. MR N CHANDRASEKARAN, EXECUTIVE VP AND HEAD OF GLOBAL OPERATIONS, TATA CONSULTANCY SERVICES: Good morning. KISHORE BELAI: Mr S Padmanabhan, Executive Vice President and Head, Global HR. MR S PADMANABHAN, EXECUTIVE VICE PRESIDENT AND HEAD, GLOBAL HR., TATA CONSULTANCY SERVICES: Good morning. KISHORE BELAI: Mr Ramadorai will present a brief overview of the company's performance for the quarter, after which we will commence the interactive session. This follows the slides are on our website and our slides will be available on the site for the rest of this quarter. As you are aware, TCS does not provide any guidance. Also I would like to remind you

that anything said on this call which reflects our outlook for the future or which can be construed as a forward-looking statement must be read in conjunction with the risk that the company faces. The full statement of this is available on the second slide in the results presentation. I now request Mr Ramadorai to present the overview. Thank you and over to Mr Ramadorai. MR S RAMADORAI: Thank you and a very very good morning to all of you and a happy Dussehra to those who celebrate it. We started with an exceptionally strong quarter performance. In terms of our overall revenues at around $1.3 billion. In terms of US GAAP we have published [gross] revenues going up by 8.93% and net income by about 8.84%. More importantly the growth has been in terms of an outstanding operational performance, multiple [rents] of large scale opportunities in a multi geography delivery model, and a multi year delivery capabilities. Whether it is the ABN Amro deal or the Tata Teleservices outsourcing contracts, these are multi million dollar, multi year deals and span multiple geographies in the case of ABN Amro. We are seeing growth in all the key areas, IT services and BPO and the [knowledge] process outsourcing, as well as areas in the infrastructure services. They are mostly be in a consulting led strategy with regard to closing some of these major deals. We added 74 new clients during this quarter and in terms of number of associates, we added almost 5,496 associates in this quarter. This does not include the additions that will come to us through the integration of Tata Infotech in the future. It's purely an organic growth in terms of associates and we were also named the best IT employer by Dataquest for the second consecutive year. I think the numbers my CEO will walk through, but more importantly, whether it is the banking financial services, retail, insurance or globalization of delivery models, what we have led as an IT services out of this country thus coming to fruition, not only for the benefit of TCS,

but also for the industry.
